correctness.rationale: The unique word decomposition into initial, internal and terminal b-gaps gives avoidance exactly when the total k in internal gaps is at most r−1: the first and last a witness any sufficient total. An internal b in gap i contributes i to the ab-count and a terminal b contributes A. Sorting the k internal gap indices and subtracting one from each gives partitions in a k by (A−2) rectangle, verifying the Gaussian factor and exponent offset, including k=0. Reversal sends C to AB−C; putting all b after the a achieves degree AB. At r=2, the k=0 and k=1 cases partition the residue classes modulo A (only k=0 when B=0). When r>B avoidance is vacuous. In the unrestricted model the weakly sorted counts of b following successive a are partitions in an A by B rectangle, with every area possible by filling rows plus one partial row; the ratio is for uniform sampling in the class. For A=2, e=(C−k)/2 and k+e≤B give the stated parity and cutoff. For even r the saturated cutoff contains equal counts of the two parities; for odd r=2s+1 the three coefficients at r−1,r,r+1 are s+1,s,s+1, also when B=r. The universal proof suffices; the packaged finite checks were inspected, not rerun.
residual_risks: The probability interpretation presupposes uniform sampling inside a Parikh class.
